children: , Google's advertising, cloud and AI parent, opened its smart-home ecosystem to rival AI agents, turning Google Home into a broader distribution platform rather than a Gemini-only playground. The shares gained approximately 1.5% to $347.91 Thursday. The valuation picture is already demanding: the stock trades 35.37% above its GF Value estimate of $257.01, suggesting investors are paying a sizable premium for Alphabet's AI and cloud growth potential.

Google's Home MCP server gives compatible AI agents the ability to inspect connected devices, track their current status, execute commands and work with historical household events. The service sits behind Google's Premium Advanced plan, priced at $20 per month or $200 annually, and also requires a Google Cloud project. Google has placed limits around higher-risk actions such as unlocking doors, but opening the system to outside agents still creates a new security variable: Google may control the infrastructure without controlling every decision made by the AI running on top of it.

The economics are more interesting than the $40 annual-plan discount. Claude, OpenClaw and other third-party agents can now funnel users deeper into Google's paid home infrastructure even when Gemini is not the interface making the decisions. That gives Alphabet another route to monetize AI interoperability instead of insisting that every interaction begin with its own model. The trade-off is straightforward: broader agent access can expand subscription demand and ecosystem reach, but one high-profile failure involving household data or device control could quickly turn an interoperability advantage into a trust problem.

title: Alphabet Gains 1.5% as $20 Opens Google Home to Rival Agents
